checks.claim: F2: Gemini Enterprise custom MCP server connections are in preview, and Pre-GA terms apply on Business edition. Requirements: Streamable HTTP only; a public IP with a publicly trusted TLS certificate and no private networking; about 100 enabled actions at most; an org-policy override. Auth is none or OAuth 2.0: the admin enters a client ID, client secret, auth and token URLs and scopes, and the redirect URI is fixed at https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/oauth-redirect.
checks.current_fact: Confirmed: search snippets from support.google.com/g/answer/17106276 say 'Creating a custom MCP Server connection is in Public Preview' and is subject to the Pre-GA Offerings Terms (admin path: Manage team > Connected apps). Snippets from Google's docs confirm Streamable HTTP only (SSE not supported), a publicly trusted TLS certificate, and a limit of 100 enabled actions. cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise/connectors lists 'Connect a custom MCP server' for both Business and Standard/Plus. Google doc snippets (Notion, Salesforce and people connectors, A2A registration) confirm the redirect URI is fixed by Google and cannot be changed. Evidence against DCR: a privacyfence GitHub issue dated 2026-09-14, citing the SecureAuth guide, says Gemini Enterprise 'supports neither Dynamic Client Registration nor OAuth discovery' and that an admin pastes a client_id and client_secret by hand. A community Gemini Enterprise MCP server also requires MCP_CLIENT_SECRET. Refuted: 'no private networking'. checks.claim: Office URI schemes: ms-word:ofe|u|<url> opens for edit, and ms-word:nft|u|<template>|s|<save-location> creates a new document from a template and saves it to a location. Only http/https URIs work, with a 256-character path limit (216 for Excel). For SharePoint/SPE, build the URI from the parent folder's webUrl plus the file name. (Plays 1 and 3)

The spec says the |s| argument only sets 'the default path offered as a save location when the file is first saved. It is possible for the user to choose a different location', and that the save location 'must be pointing to the same host name as the template'. So nft does not guarantee the new document lands in the matter folder, and the template must sit on the same SharePoint host.

No Selected scope is listed, so running them under Sites.Selected is unverified. Verify the Google files.watch channel expiry before relying on it.

play_adjustments.play_title: Tenant-side PDF conversion with LibreOffice fallback
play_adjustments.adjustment: Drop 'no metered charge' for SPE. Converting and downloading an SPE-stored file adds an API transaction plus egress on the SPE meters, paid by the firm under pass-through or by LawHand under standard billing. It stays free for regular OneDrive/SharePoint. The least-privileged application permission is Files.ReadWrite.All (write) for a read-only operation. Prefer running the conversion with the user's delegated Files.Read token at request time, or test Sites.Selected before adding app-wide write.

play_adjustments.play_title: Firm template library in SharePoint/Drive, published back as native 'New' templates
play_adjustments.adjustment: ms-word:nft|u|{template}|s|{folder} only offers a default save location that the user can change, and the location must share the template's host name. The new document may not land in the matter folder, and sync-back can miss it. A more reliable pattern: copy the template into the matter folder server-side through Graph, then launch ms-word:ofe on the copy. Graph permission tables list tenant-wide scopes for content-type provisioning (Sites.Manage.All for create/update, Sites.ReadWrite.All for copyToDefaultContentLocation), so running these under Sites.Selected needs an owner/fullcontrol grant and a test. The Selected grant itself needs Sites.FullControl.All or a SharePoint Admin, so budget an admin onboarding step. Keep LawHand templates separate from Syntex/content-assembly modern templates, because content assembly requires removing existing content controls.

play_adjustments.play_title: Native file pickers and least-privilege scopes
play_adjustments.adjustment: @googleworkspace/drive-picker-element is pre-1.0 (0.7.3, last published Dec 2025) and its GA status is unconfirmed. Pin the version or wrap the classic Picker API. Moving M365 to Sites.Selected conflicts with the Graph-subscription sync-back (Files.Read.All/Sites.Read.All documented) and with content-type provisioning. Either keep a narrowly used Files.Read.All for webhooks or accept delta polling for Selected-only tenants. Granting Selected access needs a SharePoint Admin or a Sites.FullControl.All app, so the onboarding flow needs a firm-admin step.

play_adjustments.play_title: Content-control template fields in the LawHand Word add-in
play_adjustments.adjustment: WordApi 1.9 and all WordApiDesktop sets are 'Not available' on volume-licensed perpetual/LTSC Office (Office 2024 stops at WordApi 1.8 / WordApiDesktop 1.1), which many law firms run. Make plain/rich-text content controls (WordApi 1.4–1.8) the baseline and gate everything else on isSetSupported. Use cross-platform WordApi 1.6 TrackedChange for revision review, which works in Word on the web, instead of the desktop-only WordApiDesktop 1.4 Revisions API. Add Mac 16.99.2+ to the WordApiDesktop 1.3 test matrix.

play_adjustments.play_title: Google Docs template merge path for Google-first firms
play_adjustments.adjustment: insertRichLink only creates chips for Google resources (Drive files, YouTube, Calendar), so LawHand matter links must be plain hyperlinks or come from the Workspace add-on link previews. Confirm the Drive approvals write methods are GA before building partner sign-off; only read GA is confirmed. Labels exclude Business Starter, and labels must be created and published by an admin with the Manage Labels privilege before files.modifyLabels can set them.

play_adjustments.play_title: LawHand for Google Docs (HTTP Workspace add-on)
play_adjustments.adjustment: No change to the approach: requestFileScopeForActiveDocument plus onFileScopeGranted with drive.file is confirmed for add-ons that call REST APIs. Expect a per-document authorization click in the UX.

play_adjustments.play_title: Put drafting on the client's Copilot/Gemini with LawHand as the data and skills provider
play_adjustments.adjustment: Remove the 'Cowork GA status confirmed' prerequisite and the 'Frontier' risk: Cowork went GA on 2026-06-16. Change who_pays: the client pays a Microsoft 365 Copilot license plus usage-based Copilot Credits ($0.01/credit PAYG), which makes per-run cost variable. Custom org plugins (skills plus MCP connectors) deploy through the M365 admin center; store listing needs Microsoft validation. Add the MCP-based federated Copilot connector path: it surfaces in Copilot in Word/Excel/PowerPoint/Outlook and Cowork, partner connectors need Microsoft approval, and write actions roll out from early Oct 2026. That path is a better 'Copilot in Word' route than the withdrawn agent-plus-add-in pages. For Google, the custom-MCP path runs in the Gemini Enterprise app (a separate SKU), not the Docs side panel. It requires a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint with a publicly trusted TLS certificate.

play_adjustments.play_title: Evaluate SharePoint Embedded as a 'LawHand-managed, in-tenant' storage tier (pilot only)
play_adjustments.adjustment: Run the pilot on a trial container type. Standard (non-trial) container types can't be deleted today, so the documented 'delete and re-create to change billing model' route is not available. Choosing pass-through vs standard is effectively permanent per owning app. Add the caveat that SPE-side PDF conversion and downloads to LawHand's servers count as transactions plus egress. The Copilot/Retrieval sharePointEmbedded meter is preview.

play_adjustments.play_title: Decision: do not build a WOPI host; point firm-side document automation at the firm's own PAYG
play_adjustments.adjustment: Rewrite the risk line. Per the live Learn promo page, included monthly capacity runs through December 2026, not June 2026: the public-branch copy lists 50 content-assembly docs, 100 autofill pages and 5 eSignature requests per tenant per month. PAYG prices ($0.15, $0.005/page, $2/request) are still as documented. Note that eSignature for Word needs Beta/Current/Monthly Enterprise channel and that content-assembly templates can't contain existing content controls.

checks.claim: F8 / Play 1: the 'Let Microsoft manage your consent settings' policy is the default. It rolled out July–August 2025 (MC1097272), and under it end users cannot consent to Files.Read.All, Files.ReadWrite.All, Sites.Read.All, Sites.ReadWrite.All, Mail.Read, Mail.ReadBasic, Calendars.* and similar scopes.
checks.current_fact: The current blocked list in entra-docs manage-app-consent-policies.md (ms.date 2026-01-22, repo HEAD) matches the claim. It also blocks Mail.ReadWrite, the *.Shared variants, MailboxItem.Read, MailBoxFolder.*, MailBoxSettings.*, OnlineMeetings.*, Tasks.* and the Exchange Online permissions EAS, EWS, IMAP and POP.AccessAsUser.All. The timeline in the claim is wrong. MC1097272 (July to August 2025) blocked only the four Files and Sites .All permissions. Mail, Calendars, Chat, Contacts, Tasks and People were added in a later update that started at the end of October 2025 (MC1163922). More Exchange permissions followed from June 2026 (MC1304287). The policy only affects tenants that use the Microsoft-managed policy; tenants with custom policies are not affected. A separate 'Mail client policy' lets users consent only for named mail clients (Apple Mail, Spark, eM Client), not for ISVs such as LawHand. Mail.Send, Files.Read, Files.ReadWrite and User.Read are not on the blocked list, so users can still consent to them.

checks.claim: F9 / F17 / Play 1 and 6: in the admin consent workflow only Global Administrators can approve requests for Microsoft Graph app roles. In the Integrated Apps deploy flow, only a Global Admin can accept permissions. Deployment targets top-level groups only (not nested groups), and Teams apps need unified manifest 1.13 or later to run in Outlook and the M365 app.
checks.current_fact: Confirmed. configure-admin-consent-workflow.md (ms.date 2024-12-29) says reviewers can view, block or deny requests, 'but only Global Administrators can approve admin consent requests for apps requesting for Microsoft Graph app roles'. teams-apps-work-on-outlook-and-m365.md (ms.date 2025-08-26) says 'If the app needs consent, select Accept permissions. Only a global administrator can give consent.' test-and-deploy-microsoft-365-apps.md confirms the top-level-group rule and the manifest 1.13 split. That doc also says the Integrated Apps portal is 'available to world-wide customers only' and 'not available in sovereign and government clouds'.

checks.claim: F0 / Play 2: maximum Graph subscription lifetimes are 10,080 min for Outlook message, event and contact (1,440 min with rich notifications) and 42,300 min for driveItem and list. Requests above the maximum will fail in the future.
checks.current_fact: This matches the include change-notifications-subscription-lifetime.md exactly (ms.date 2024-11-07, repo HEAD), including the note 'In the future, any requests to create or renew a subscription beyond the maximum value will fail.' That table also says todoTask webhooks are not available in national clouds.

checks.claim: F1 / F2 / Play 2: webhook delivery counts only after a 2xx within 3 s. Retries run for up to 4 h with a 10 s timeout. An endpoint is marked 'slow' at more than 10% over 3 s and 'drop' at more than 15% over 10 s, and dropped notifications are unrecoverable. The recommended pattern is to validate, enqueue and return 202. Lifecycle events: reauthorizationRequired applies to all resources; subscriptionRemoved and missed apply only to Outlook (subscriptionRemoved also to Teams chatMessage).
checks.current_fact: Confirmed word for word in change-notifications-delivery-webhooks.md (ms.date 2025-01-15) and change-notifications-lifecycle-events.md. driveItem and list get only reauthorizationRequired, never 'missed', so periodic delta sweeps are the only recovery path for files.

checks.claim: F4 / Plays 3 and 8: a message subscription accepts delegated Mail.ReadBasic or Mail.Read. A driveItem subscription on OneDrive for Business needs Files.Read.All and can only be on the root folder. A list subscription needs Sites.Read.All. 'prefer: includesecuritywebhooks' sends notifications when permissions change.
checks.current_fact: Confirmed in subscription-post-subscriptions.md (ms.date 2024-10-28). The permission table lists no Sites.Selected or Files.SelectedOperations.Selected option for driveItem or list. The conclusion that a Sites.Selected-only app cannot use drive or list webhooks is an inference from that table and should be tested in a dev tenant.

checks.claim: F10 / F11 / F12 / Play 3: selected scopes need three steps (Entra consent, a POST to /permissions, and the scope in the token). Granting at site level needs Sites.FullControl.All. Delegated Sites.Selected needs no admin consent, but delegated Files.SelectedOperations.Selected does. Sites.Create.All auto-grants Sites.Selected plus FullControl on the new site. POST /sites exists only in beta. Delegated Mail.ReadBasic does not need admin consent.
checks.status: Selected scopes GA; POST /sites beta only (v1.0 page returns 404)
checks.current_fact: Confirmed in permissions-selected-overview.md and in the permissions-reference.md entries: Sites.Selected is admin consent Yes (application) and No (delegated); Files.SelectedOperations.Selected and Lists.SelectedOperations.Selected are Yes and Yes; Sites.Create.All is Yes and Yes, and its description is 'granted Sites.Selected + FullControl to the newly created site'; Mail.ReadBasic is Yes (application) and No (delegated). The beta site-post-sites.md carries the beta disclaimer (ms.date 2025-10-09), and api-reference/v1.0/api/site-post-sites.md does not exist. Mail.ReadBasic is 'no admin consent required' only in principle: the Microsoft-managed policy still blocks user consent to it.

checks.claim: F13 / Play 3: RBAC for Applications in Exchange Online replaces Application Access Policies, which are now labelled legacy, and no retirement date has been published. Microsoft blocks non-Microsoft apps from using EWS against Exchange Online from 2026-10-01.
checks.status: GA (RBAC for Apps); EWS retirement in progress
checks.current_fact: The Learn page is titled 'Application Access Policies (legacy)', and no retirement date appears in results (a community post from July 2026 says the same). On EWS: from 1 October 2026, tenants whose EWSEnabled is still null are switched to False, which blocks EWS. Admins who set up an AppID allow list (deadline around the end of August 2026) can keep access until EWS is permanently disabled on 1 April 2027. LawHand does not use EWS, so this is informational only. From search snippets only; the Exchange doc repos are not public on GitHub and learn.microsoft.com is blocked.

checks.claim: F15 / F16 / Play 6: publisher verification is free and needs a verified Cloud Partner Program account plus a matching publisher domain. Publisher Attestation is a self-assessment of about 1 hour and is required for all Teams apps.
checks.current_fact: publisher-verification-overview.md says 'Microsoft doesn't charge developers for publisher verification. No license is required.' It requires a partner global account (PGA) Partner One ID, not a location ID, and a publisher domain that is not *.onmicrosoft.com. Learn snippets confirm 'Publisher Attestation is a requirement for all Teams apps' and 'Most attestations can be completed in one hour or less', filled in through Partner Center, and Microsoft does not independently verify the answers. Attestation is tied to Partner Center (store or AppSource) submissions. Attestation content comes from search snippets only; the M365 certification doc repo is not public.

checks.claim: F19 / Play 2: Gmail users.watch must be renewed at least every 7 days (Google recommends daily). The Pub/Sub topic must be in the same GCP project, and gmail-api-push@system.gserviceaccount.com needs publish rights. Each user is capped at about 1 notification per second. watch and history.list accept gmail.metadata.
checks.current_fact: The Gmail discovery document (rev 20260917) describes WatchRequest.topicName as: the 'my-project-identifier' portion 'must exactly match your Google developer project id (the one executing this watch request)'. The watch and history.list scopes include gmail.metadata, gmail.readonly, gmail.modify and mail.google.com. The q parameter 'cannot be used when accessing the api using the gmail.metadata scope'. Search snippets of the official push guide confirm the 7-day and daily renewal and the gmail-api-push publisher grant. The official guide says notifications over 1/sec are dropped; one third-party guide says 'batched or delayed', so the history.list fallback sweep is still needed.

checks.claim: F22 / Plays 2 and 8: Google Drive subscriptions in the Workspace Events API are generally available (developer preview in July 2025). They cover files added or moved, edits and revisions, trash and untrash, access proposals and comments.
checks.current_fact: A search snippet of the Workspace Events release notes says 'Subscriptions are now generally available for Google Drive events', dated May 18, 2026, and a Q2 2026 roundup headline says 'Drive Events GA'. The v1 discovery document (rev 20260906) has no Developer Preview marker for Drive; the only preview is org-wide Chat subscriptions. It includes DriveOptions.includeDescendants and accepts the drive, drive.file, drive.readonly, drive.metadata and drive.metadata.readonly scopes. The July 2025 event list confirms added/moved, edited/revision, trash/untrash and access proposal; the claimed 'comments' event type could not be confirmed. developers.google.com is blocked, so this rests on the discovery document and snippets.

checks.claim: F25 / Play 5: restricted scopes need restricted-scope verification plus a CASA 'Tier 2' assessment by a Google-authorized lab, redone every 12 months from the Letter of Assessment date. The cost is about $540–$1,800 per year.
checks.current_fact: The 12-month reassessment from the LOA approval date is confirmed in a snippet of Google's restricted-scope verification page. The naming is out of date: the App Defense Alliance CASA Specification v2.1.1 (2026-06-03, ADA ASA-WG GitHub) replaces tiers with 'ADA Assurance Level 1 (Verified Self Assessment, lab reviews evidence)' and 'Assurance Level 2 (Lab Assessment, lab tests the app directly)', and the program is now described as the ADA Application Security Assessment. Google assigns the level. Third parties disagree on whether restricted-scope multi-tenant apps land at AL1 or AL2, and on price ($500–$4,500 depending on level). The $540–$1,800 figure is third-party and applies to the old Tier 2.

checks.claim: F26 / F27 / F28 / Play 5: drive.file is non-sensitive and grants per-file access through Picker. A Testing-status app is capped at 100 test users and its refresh tokens expire in 7 days. An unverified production app shows a warning and has a 100-user cap. Admins can trust an unverified app for their domain.
checks.current_fact: drive.file is confirmed non-sensitive with per-file and Picker access; Google recommends migrating from restricted Drive scopes to it (Drive scope guide snippet). The Drive discovery document (rev 20260916) lists drive.file for changes.watch and changes.list. The 7-day refresh-token expiry applies to projects with an External user type in Testing status (Manage App Audience help snippet). A clarification the play needs: when a Workspace admin marks an app as Trusted in API controls, Google treats it as internal for that org, so its users see no unverified-app screen and are not subject to the 100-user cap. That applies to an app in production that is unverified, not to one in Testing, which still allows only listed test users with 7-day tokens. Admin-help content comes from search snippets because support.google.com is blocked.

checks.claim: F23 / Play 3: Google Calendar offers granular scopes (calendar.events.owned, calendar.events.owned.readonly, calendar.app.created, calendar.calendarlist, calendar.events.freebusy) usable with events.watch and a syncToken.
checks.current_fact: The Calendar discovery document (rev 20260826) lists all of these scopes. events.watch and events.list accept calendar.app.created, calendar.events.owned and calendar.events.owned.readonly. events.insert accepts calendar.app.created and calendar.events.owned. 'owned' covers only calendars the user owns, not shared or delegated calendars.

checks.claim: F6 / F7 / Play 7: Outlook limits are 10,000 requests per 10 min and 4 concurrent requests per app per mailbox. Subscription writes are limited to 500 per 20 s per app per tenant. SharePoint charges 1 RU for delta with a token (2 without). The ISV User-Agent format is 'ISV|CompanyName|AppName/Version', and decorated traffic is prioritized.
checks.current_fact: The limits are confirmed in throttling-outlook.md and throttling-subscription-services.md (per app per tenant: 500 writes per 20 s, 25 list reads per 20 s) and in how-to-avoid-getting-throttled-or-blocked-in-sharepoint-online.md (ms.date 2025-10-02): 1,250 RU per minute and 1.2M RU per 24 h for 0–1,000 licenses, and 'Well-decorated traffic will be prioritized'. The User-Agent guidance is SharePoint-specific and also asks for a registered AppID and AppTitle.

play_adjustments.play_title: Admin-first Microsoft onboarding (tenant-wide admin consent + 'Pending admin approval' state)
play_adjustments.adjustment: 1) Fix the timeline: MC1097272 (July–August 2025) blocked only Files and Sites .All. Mail, Calendars, Chat, Contacts, Tasks and People were blocked from the end of October 2025 (MC1163922), and Exchange EAS, EWS, IMAP and POP from June 2026 (MC1304287). Replace the risk 'tenants consented before July 2025 behave differently' with: existing grants stay valid; new users and broader scopes in tenants on the Microsoft-managed policy need an admin; tenants on custom consent policies are unaffected. 2) Users can still self-consent to Mail.Send, Files.Read, Files.ReadWrite (their own OneDrive), User.Read and offline_access. Per-user send and own-file features can therefore stay self-serve, and only the mail, calendar and tenant-file read tiers wait for an admin. 3) Say which admin role is needed. Integrated Apps 'Accept permissions' requires a Global Admin, and so does approving admin-consent-workflow requests for Graph application permissions. The copyable link should say which role to send it to. 4) The 'Mail client policy' allow-list does not cover third-party ISVs, so do not suggest it as a workaround. 5) Integrated Apps is worldwide-cloud only.

play_adjustments.play_title: Replace polling with event-driven sync (Graph subscriptions + delta; Gmail watch + history; Drive/Workspace Events; Calendar watch + syncToken)
play_adjustments.adjustment: The core facts hold (lifetimes, 3 s/202 receiver, lifecycle events, Gmail 7-day watch). Workspace Events Drive subscriptions are GA as of May 2026 (release-notes snippet); do not rely on a 'comments' event type until it is confirmed. The Gmail Pub/Sub topic's project ID must exactly match the GCP project that runs users.watch, so LawHand cannot use a topic in another project. For driveItem and list, Graph sends no 'missed' lifecycle events, and OneDrive for Business subscriptions are root-only. The nightly and on-notification delta sweep is therefore the recovery mechanism, not a fallback. If Play 5 moves Drive to drive.file, test whether Workspace Events folder subscriptions with includeDescendants deliver events or resources for child files the app was never granted through Picker.

play_adjustments.play_title: Least-privilege scope tiers mapped to features (incremental consent)
play_adjustments.adjustment: 1) Delegated Mail.ReadBasic is still blocked by the Microsoft-managed policy, so it gives no consent benefit over Mail.Read in those tenants. It is a data-minimization choice only; justify it that way or drop it. 2) Remove 'or Sites.Create.All once POST /sites is GA'. POST /sites is still beta only (no v1.0 page), so plan on the one-time Sites.Selected grant. Granting at site level needs Sites.FullControl.All (or an admin using the SharePoint admin tooling), and all three steps must be done. 3) RBAC for Applications only narrows access if the tenant-wide Entra application Mail.Read grant is removed. Entra and Exchange RBAC grants are additive, so an unscoped Entra app role still reaches every mailbox. 4) Google calendar.events.owned and calendar.app.created are confirmed and work with events.watch and events.list; note that owned excludes shared and delegated calendars.

play_adjustments.play_title: Google launch path decision: drive.file-first, restricted-scope CASA only if Gmail reading is core
play_adjustments.adjustment: 1) Rename 'CASA Tier 2'. The ADA CASA Specification v2.1.1 (2026-06-03) uses Assurance Level 1 (lab-reviewed self-assessment) and Assurance Level 2 (lab-run assessment), and Google assigns the level. Budget for AL2, because the $540–$1,800 figure is third-party and applies to the old Tier 2; third parties now quote $500–$4,500. 2) Phase 1 pilots should run with the OAuth app in 'In production' status (unverified) and each customer admin marking it Trusted in API controls. Google then treats it as internal for that org: no unverified-app screen and no 100-user cap. Do not pilot in 'Testing' status, which allows only listed test users and expires refresh tokens after 7 days for External apps. The phrase 'internal 100-user and 7-day testing limits' conflates the Internal user type with Testing status. 3) Before committing, confirm that picking a folder with Picker under drive.file gives the access the matter-folder model needs (child files and events).

play_adjustments.play_title: Microsoft trust signals: publisher verification + Publisher Attestation now, M365 Certification later; ship via Integrated Apps
play_adjustments.adjustment: Publisher verification (free, PGA Partner One ID, publisher domain not onmicrosoft.com) and Attestation (at most about 1 hour, required for Teams apps) both check out. Attestation is filed through Partner Center for store or AppSource listings, so badges appear only if LawHand's Teams app, add-in or SaaS app is published there, not if firms side-load or upload it as a custom or LOB app. Sequence the store submission before counting on badges in the Integrated Apps Security & Compliance tab. Integrated Apps deploy and consent needs a Global Admin, and the portal does not exist in sovereign or government clouds.

play_adjustments.play_title: Matter-file permission-change alerts (ethical walls)
play_adjustments.adjustment: The Microsoft half holds: 'prefer: includesecuritywebhooks' on a Files.Read.All subscription at the drive root, for OneDrive for Business and SharePoint only. The Google half needs correcting. Drive 'access proposal' events report that someone requested access; they do not report actual sharing or permission changes. To detect real permission changes on Google, diff permissions from changes.list or the Drive Activity API, or use the Admin SDK Reports Drive audit log (needs admin authorization). Keep the Workspace Events access-proposal subscription as an extra signal, not the main one.

play_adjustments.play_title: Graph/SharePoint throttling hygiene
play_adjustments.adjustment: The numbers hold. The User-Agent 'ISV|LawHand|LawHand/<version>' rule and the traffic prioritization are documented for SharePoint Online APIs; setting the header on Graph is harmless but the prioritization is not promised there. The doc also asks ISVs to use a registered AppID and AppTitle. Subscription writes are limited to 500 per 20 s per app per tenant, so a firm-wide renewal pass for large tenants must be rate-limited.

play_adjustments.play_title: National cloud readiness (defer until demand)
play_adjustments.adjustment: Add that the M365 admin center Integrated Apps portal is not available in sovereign or government clouds, so the Play 6 one-flow admin deploy does not exist for GCC High or DoD. Those tenants need Teams admin center or centralized deployment plus a separate /adminconsent flow against login.microsoftonline.us. todoTask webhooks are global-only, as the play already says.

checks.claim: Microsoft's Legal Agent in Word (Microsoft 365 Copilot) is in Frontier preview only (US from 2026-04-30, worldwide Frontier from mid-June 2026). GA has slipped twice and is now set for early October 2026 per MC1388706. It needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence plus Frontier enrollment, with nothing to install. The research also says there is no evidence it can use third-party playbooks.
checks.current_fact: Status and licensing hold. Per MC1388706 (updated 2026-08-24), Frontier preview runs from mid-June 2026 and GA is 'early October 2026 (previously early September)'. It needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, is on by default for tenants in Frontier, needs no separate installation, and does not affect tenants outside Frontier. As of 2026-09-24 it is still preview. The claim that it has no route for firm playbooks is wrong: several secondary sources say a playbook is an ordinary Word document kept in OneDrive or SharePoint, which the agent reviews clauses against. One secondary source says it ran only in Word for Windows desktop at launch. Method: mc.merill.net, handsontek, cloudscout and support.microsoft.com were all blocked by the proxy, so this rests on search-result snippets of those pages.

checks.claim: Copilot Cowork became generally available on 2026-06-16 with nine partner plugins, Harvey among them. The research left licence tier and plugin requirements unconfirmed, and play 3 assumes the customer's Copilot seat pays for the Copilot-side reasoning.
checks.current_fact: The GA date and partner list hold. The nine plugins available now are Enosix, Harvey, LSEG, Miro, monday.com, Moody's, Morningstar, S&P Global Energy and TeamsMaestro; eight more are coming (Adobe, Atlassian, Box, Canva, CB Insights, Databricks, MoneyForward, Templafy). Licensing is not what the play assumes. Per the primary Microsoft 365 blog, which I fetched directly, Cowork 'requires the Microsoft 365 Copilot User Subscription License (USL)', and users are then 'billed for Cowork on a usage-based basis' in Copilot Credits: PayGo is $0.01 per credit, or P3 prepurchase at a discount. No allowance is included. 'Cowork is off by default'; admins enable it and choose who gets it, with spending caps at tenant, group and user level. On developer requirements, the MicrosoftDocs m365copilot-docs file plugin-authentication.md (ms.date 2026-08-12) says 'Cowork MCP plugins' use the same auth model as MCP plugins for declarative agents.

checks.claim: Who pays in play 3: the customer's Microsoft 365 Copilot seat covers Copilot-side reasoning for a LawHand agent (the NetDocuments model), and LawHand covers only its own tool calls.
checks.current_fact: This holds for declarative agents used by licensed users. MicrosoftDocs m365copilot-docs cost-considerations.md (ms.date 2026-06-18) says: 'For users with Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licenses, no extra charges', even when the agent has actions, plugins or connectors. It does not hold in two cases. (1) Users without a Copilot licence: an agent grounded in shared tenant data (SharePoint, Copilot connectors) is billed in Copilot Credits. (2) Every Cowork task is billed in Copilot Credits on top of the USL.

checks.claim: Harvey runs as an agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot (@Harvey or the sidebar, grounded in Harvey Vault) and as a Copilot Cowork plugin. Users are believed to need both a Harvey subscription and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
checks.status: GA (agent + Cowork plugin); federated connectors listed
checks.current_fact: The core claim holds. A search snippet of Harvey's help page says: 'To use Harvey for Copilot, you'll need an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license and a Harvey subscription.' There is also a Harvey SaaS listing on Microsoft Marketplace (WA200007562). Harvey is additionally listed as a federated (MCP) Copilot connector in Microsoft's gallery: 'Harvey' under Legal, plus 'Harvey AU (preview)' and 'Harvey EU (preview)'. So the reference pattern is agent plus Cowork plugin plus federated connector, not the agent alone. I did not independently verify the 'since March 2026' date or the July 2026 adoption by Microsoft's legal department (CELA). Method: help.harvey.ai and the marketplace were blocked, so this uses search snippets plus the MicrosoftDocs copilot-connectors GitHub repo.

checks.claim: NetDocuments sells 'NetDocuments Copilot' as a Microsoft Marketplace SaaS offer (US WA200008488, CAN WA200008857). It needs both a Microsoft 365 Copilot subscription and a NetDocuments subscription, respects ethical walls, and is available in North America.
checks.current_fact: The claim holds, with refinements. Per search snippets of the listings, 'NetDocuments Copilot requires both Microsoft 365 Copilot and NetDocuments subscriptions'. The US offer covers 'North, Central and South America', and there are separate regional offers, for example DE (WA200008865) and AU. Each regional app has a Microsoft 365 App Certification record, filed under Teams, which confirms the certification program is still active in 2026. Customers are told to buy ndMAX through their account executive. The marketplace and Learn pages were blocked, so this rests on snippets.

checks.claim: Microsoft documents an 'iManage Cloud connector (preview)', a synced Copilot connector that indexes iManage workspaces, documents and metadata into the tenant. Play 6 copies this ingest-into-the-tenant pattern.

checks.current_fact: The name is current: all Microsoft docs now say 'Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors'. The research missed that there are two models. Synced connectors index content into Microsoft Graph. Federated connectors are MCP-based and 'retrieve content in real time ... without indexing data into Microsoft Graph', 'access data using the user's identity and permissions', and can be published by Microsoft or submitted by partners and approved by Microsoft. They run in Copilot Chat, Agents, Cowork, Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, and Researcher. Create, update and delete actions start rolling out in early October 2026 and need the user's approval; Researcher stays read-only. On Agent 365, it is no longer unknown: per search snippets of the Microsoft Tech Community post and licensing guides, it went GA together with Microsoft 365 E7 ('Frontier Suite', GA 2026-05-01, $99 per user per month). checks.claim: Play 1 risk: a Gmail add-on on current-message scopes may avoid Gmail's restricted-scope classification and the security assessment that comes with it.
checks.current_fact: This holds. Per search snippets of Google's Gmail API scopes table, 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.addons.current.message.readonly' ('View your email messages when the add-on is running') is classified as Sensitive, not Restricted. That means standard OAuth app verification but no CASA assessment. It grants temporary access to the open message and the other messages in its thread. By contrast, gmail.readonly and gmail.metadata are Restricted, and the mailbox-wide auto-filing in play 2 needs them, so CASA would apply there with annual re-certification. From my own knowledge, not verified this session: putting a visible Gmail label on a message goes through messages.modify, which needs gmail.modify (Restricted). developers.google.com was blocked, so this rests on snippets.

checks.claim: Office.js prerequisites for plays 1 and 4. Play 1: item access through 'the current item's REST/Graph token or getAsFileAsync'. Play 4: the WordApi change-tracking requirement set, used for a new insert_with_tracking action.
checks.current_fact: Word: Document.changeTrackingMode is 'API set: WordApi 1.4'. TrackedChange and TrackedChangeCollection (read, accept, reject) are 'WordApi 1.6'. So insert_with_tracking (turn on trackAll, then insert) needs only 1.4, while reviewing redlines needs 1.6 (office-js-docs-reference word_1_6 YAML). Outlook: getAsFileAsync is Mailbox 1.14 with read-item permission, and getAttachmentContentAsync is Mailbox 1.8. For Exchange Online, Microsoft's documented fallback is Microsoft Graph with a token from nested app authentication (NAA), using convertToRestId for the item ID (get-attachments-of-an-outlook-item.md, ms.date 2026-09-01). The 'REST token' route is the obsolete legacy-Exchange-token pattern that Microsoft's NAA sample replaces. LawHand's office-addin/manifests/outlook.xml declares a minimum of Mailbox 1.3, so the new actions need runtime isSetSupported checks or a higher minimum.

play_adjustments.play_title: Publish the LawHand Matter Agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot and as a Copilot Cowork plugin
play_adjustments.adjustment:
1. Correct who pays. Declarative agents add no charge for Copilot-licensed users. Cowork requires the Copilot USL and is also billed per task in Copilot Credits ($0.01 per credit PayGo, or P3 prepurchase), and it is off by default until an admin enables it. Change who_pays_compute for Cowork to 'client Copilot USL + client metered Copilot Credits + LawHand MCP'. Unlicensed users of agents grounded in tenant data are also metered.
2. Add a first step that is cheaper and reaches more surfaces: submit LawHand's Workspace MCP as a partner federated Copilot connector through Partner Center. It then works in Chat, Agents, Cowork, Researcher, and Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook. Microsoft names 'matter management' as a legal use case, and Harvey, iManage Work, Relativity and Everlaw are already listed.
3. Constraints for that submission: every submitted tool needs readOnlyHint (a read-only tool profile, with propose_* excluded); a public HTTPS endpoint; an OAuth 2.0 client ID and secret registered in the Teams Developer Portal (DCR is not listed for connectors, though it is supported for declarative-agent and Cowork MCP plugins); a reviewer test account; and three or more sample prompts.
4. propose_* tools can follow once federated write actions roll out (early October 2026). Those require user confirmation, are audited in Purview, and do not run in Researcher.

play_adjustments.play_title: Metadata-only Microsoft 365 Copilot connector for matter resolution (optional, enterprise tier)
play_adjustments.adjustment: Rework this play. The synced 'iManage Cloud connector (preview)' page it models was redirected away in August 2026. It had been a private, allow-listed preview, and iManage now appears as 'iManage Work (preview)', a federated (MCP) connector. Rebuild the play as a federated connector: a read-only matter lookup and resolve tool on the existing Workspace MCP. It needs no indexing into Microsoft Graph, runs as the user with that user's permissions, and requires admin approval. That removes the main risks the play lists: data residency, privilege disclosure, ACL drift and ethical-wall mapping. It also likely drops effort from L to M and can merge with play 3's connector submission. Keep a synced connector only as an option for customers who explicitly want semantic-index recall.
